questions.stem: Statement: 'Students who study regularly perform better in exams.' Assumption I: Regular study improves academic performance. Assumption II: All students who perform well study more than 8 hours daily. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is implicit — the statement is premised on regular study helping performance. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement makes no claim about '8 hours daily'; that specific figure is an addition, not an unstated premise.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'If you want to lose weight, exercise regularly.' Assumption I: Everyone wants to lose weight. Assumption II: Regular exercise helps in losing weight. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — the statement is conditional ('if you want to'), so it does not assume everyone desires weight loss. Assumption II IS implicit — the advice to exercise for weight loss is premised on exercise being effective for that purpose.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The government should build more hospitals to improve healthcare.' Assumption I: The current number of hospitals is insufficient. Assumption II: More hospitals will improve healthcare access and quality. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is implicit — the call to build 'more' hospitals assumes the existing number is inadequate. Assumption II is implicit — the prescription that building hospitals improves healthcare assumes a causal link. Both are required premises. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Ramesh reads the newspaper every morning.' Assumption I: The newspaper is the only source of information for Ramesh. Assumption II: Ramesh reads the newspaper at home. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Neither assumption is implicit. Assumption I overstates exclusivity — the statement says nothing about other sources. Assumption II specifies location ('home') which the statement does not — he could read at a café, workplace, etc. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Please carry an umbrella as it may rain today.' Assumption I: An umbrella provides protection against rain. Assumption II: It will definitely rain today. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — advising to carry an umbrella for rain protection assumes the umbrella will protect. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement says 'may rain' (uncertain), so definite rain is not assumed. → Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Eating fresh fruits and vegetables is important for good health.' Assumption I: All health problems can be solved by eating fruits and vegetables. Assumption II: Fresh fruits and vegetables contain nutrients necessary for health. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — 'important' does not mean 'sufficient for all problems'; it overstates the claim. Assumption II IS implicit — asserting fruits and vegetables are important for health assumes they contain what the body needs. → Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Donate to this charity to help the flood victims.' Assumption I: The charity uses donations to help flood victims. Assumption II: There are flood victims who need assistance. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — the donation appeal assumes the charity will actually direct funds to victims. Assumption II IS implicit — asking people to donate to 'help flood victims' assumes such victims exist and need help. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'India should increase its defence budget to ensure national security.' Assumption I: India currently has no military forces. Assumption II: Increasing the defence budget will solve all security threats. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is clearly wrong and not implicit — India has a military. Assumption II overstates ('all threats'); the statement says 'ensure' national security broadly, not that all threats vanish. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Switch to our toothpaste brand for a brighter smile.' (Advertisement) Assumption I: This toothpaste can help make teeth appear brighter. Assumption II: No other toothpaste brand can make teeth bright. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — promising a brighter smile assumes the product can deliver that result. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the ad says 'switch to our brand' but makes no claim that rival brands cannot whiten teeth. → Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The city should invest in public transportation to reduce traffic congestion.' Assumption I: Traffic congestion will disappear completely if public transport improves. Assumption II: Good public transportation encourages commuters to shift from private vehicles, thereby reducing congestion. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — 'reduce' ≠ 'eliminate completely'; the statement is modest in its claim. Assumption II IS implicit — the proposal assumes the mechanism: better public transport → reduced private vehicle usage → reduced congestion. → Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Parents should encourage their children to read books from an early age.' Assumption I: Reading books from an early age benefits children's development. Assumption II: Children can be influenced by their parents' encouragement. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — the advice to encourage early reading assumes it is beneficial. Assumption II IS implicit — telling parents to 'encourage' children assumes that such encouragement has a positive effect on children's behaviour. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Scientists have discovered a new species of bird in the Amazon rainforest.' Assumption I: The Amazon rainforest had been completely explored before this discovery. Assumption II: This new species exists exclusively in the Amazon and nowhere else. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — a new discovery does not imply prior complete exploration; it just means the species was not known before. Assumption II is NOT implicit — being discovered in the Amazon does not mean it cannot exist elsewhere. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Wear sunscreen before going out in the sun to protect your skin.' Assumption I: Sunscreen protects the skin from harmful effects of sun exposure. Assumption II: Going out in the sun is always harmful to everyone. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — advising sunscreen for protection assumes it works as a protective agent. Assumption II is NOT implicit — 'to protect your skin' implies potential risk, not that sun exposure is universally and always harmful. → Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The company has decided to give all employees a performance bonus this quarter.' Assumption I: All employees deserve a bonus every quarter without exception. Assumption II: The company has sufficient funds to pay performance bonuses this quarter. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — the company made a specific quarter decision; it doesn't assume bonuses are owed every quarter. Assumption II IS implicit — if the company decided to pay bonuses, it must be assumed they have the financial means to do so. → Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The teacher advised students to attempt the easier questions first in the examination.' Assumption I: Some questions in the examination are easier than others. Assumption II: Attempting easier questions first helps students manage time or gain confidence. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — if all questions were equally difficult, the advice to do 'easier ones first' would be meaningless. Assumption II IS implicit — the advice is premised on the belief that this strategy offers some advantage (time management or confidence). → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Mobile phones have become an essential part of modern life.' Assumption I: People cannot survive without mobile phones. Assumption II: Mobile phones were equally essential to life 50 years ago. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I overstates — 'essential part of modern life' means very useful/integrated, not literally indispensable for survival. Assumption II is factually false (phones didn't exist 50 years ago) and not implicit. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Travellers are advised to book train tickets well in advance.' Assumption I: Train tickets may not be available if booked at the last moment. Assumption II: Train is the only mode of transport available for travellers. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — advising advance booking makes sense only if last-minute availability cannot be guaranteed (trains can get fully booked). Assumption II is NOT implicit — the advice is only about train tickets, not about the existence or absence of other transport options. → Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'A notice outside a factory: Wear helmets and safety gear at all times in the production area.' Assumption I: Workers in the production area never face accidents when not wearing safety gear. Assumption II: Safety gear reduces the risk of injury in industrial accidents. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I contradicts the intent of the notice — the notice implies there IS risk; it is NOT implicit. Assumption II IS implicit — mandating safety gear assumes it provides protection and reduces injury risk. → Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The principal announced that school will remain closed tomorrow due to heavy rainfall.' Assumption I: Heavy rainfall poses a safety risk or hardship for students travelling to school. Assumption II: The closure announcement can be communicated to students and parents in time for them to act on it. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — closing school due to rain assumes rain creates some problem for students (safety, transport difficulty). Assumption II IS implicit — making an announcement assumes it will reach the intended audience in time to be useful. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Online shopping has increased significantly since the launch of several e-commerce platforms.' Assumption I: People preferred offline shopping over online shopping before e-commerce platforms existed. Assumption II: E-commerce platforms will eventually replace all physical retail stores. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — an increase in online shopping since e-commerce launched does not mean offline was preferred before; other factors matter. Assumption II is a future prediction not contained in the statement, so NOT implicit. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Despite rising costs of living, middle-class families in Tier-2 cities save a higher percentage of income than those in Tier-1 cities.' Assumption I: The cost of living in Tier-2 cities is relatively lower than in Tier-1 cities, enabling higher savings rates. Assumption II: Middle-class families across all city tiers have identical income levels. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — higher savings rates despite 'rising costs' makes most sense if Tier-2 expenses are comparatively lower than Tier-1, leaving more to save. Assumption II is NOT implicit — the statement compares savings rates, not incomes; it is also generally false that all city tiers earn identically. → Only I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The government should impose higher taxes on luxury goods to fund public health schemes.' Assumption I: Consumers of luxury goods will stop purchasing them if taxes are raised. Assumption II: Revenue from higher taxes on luxury goods can be channelled to fund public health schemes. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — the proposal is to generate revenue to fund schemes, not to discourage purchases; even if some buyers continue, tax revenue is earned. Assumption II IS implicit — the logic of the statement depends on luxury-tax revenue being usable for health schemes. → Only II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The Supreme Court ruled that the right to a clean environment is a fundamental right under Article 21.' Assumption I: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution is broad enough to be interpreted as encompassing environmental rights. Assumption II: Citizens may approach the court for legal remedy if their right to a clean environment is violated. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — the ruling is based on a broad interpretation of Article 21; without this, the ruling would have no constitutional basis. Assumption II IS implicit — declaring something a fundamental right implies enforceable legal protection, i.e., the right to seek a remedy. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Experts recommend that workers take a short break every hour to prevent repetitive strain injuries.' Assumption I: All workers who work continuously for more than one hour will definitely develop strain injuries. Assumption II: Taking breaks more frequently than once per hour is harmful to workers. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is NOT implicit — 'prevent' indicates a precautionary recommendation, not a certainty that injury will occur without breaks. Assumption II is NOT implicit — recommending one break per hour does not imply more frequent breaks are harmful; the statement sets a minimum, not a maximum. → Neither I nor II.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The Finance Minister stated that reducing corporate tax rates will attract more foreign investment and boost economic growth.' Assumption I: Foreign investors factor in the tax rate of a country when deciding where to invest. Assumption II: An increase in foreign investment leads to economic growth. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I IS implicit — if tax rates didn't influence investment decisions, reducing them wouldn't attract investment. Assumption II IS implicit — the chain 'tax cut → more investment → economic growth' requires that increased foreign investment actually drives growth. → Both I and II.
questions.subject: Reasoning
